scholarships.title: Chevening SIDS Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Chevening (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office scheme)

eligibility: To be eligible for a Chevening SIDS Scholarship, you must meet the standard eligibility criteria for Chevening, and be a citizen from one of the participating countries shown on the map on the official page.
Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.

If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country. This does not have to be the country of citizenship, but all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours.

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme. You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate; you will need the certificate by the time of your interview.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses, and receive an unconditional offer from at least one by the deadline listed on the application timeline.

Applicants are required to study on courses that help to address a national development priority or capacity shortage. This includes courses relating to: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives.
existing.eligibility_summary: Must meet the standard Chevening eligibility criteria and be a citizen of a participating SIDS country, and must study on a course addressing a national development priority or capacity shortage.
benefits: Full tuition fees for a one-year UK master's degree at the university of the scholar's choice
A monthly stipend, stated in the Final Award Letter, which Chevening says is intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights between the nearest airport in the home country and the nearest airport to the UK university, booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge ('you don't need to pay the visa fee or the Immigration Health Surcharge')
Arrival allowance where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Departure allowance for scholars on a full award

requirements: Applications must be submitted through the Chevening online application system reached from your own country/territory page.
Opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship within the standard Chevening Scholarship application.
Choose three different eligible UK master's degree courses in order of preference; duplicate courses at the same university cannot be considered.
Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses (not research-focused MRes programmes), based in the UK, starting in the autumn term (usually September/October) and lasting nine to twelve months.
Courses cannot be part-time, distance learning, a PhD or DPhil, or include more than one month of study outside the UK.
Provide the names and contact details of two referees in the application.
If shortlisted, upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate to the online application system no later than seven working days before your interview.
If successful at interview, submit at least one unconditional UK university offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
Apply for your own student visa; Chevening cannot apply on your behalf.
documents: Two reference letters written by your nominated referees in English (uploaded only if you progress to interview)

Your undergraduate degree certificate - 'This must be an official document from your university proving your degree and grade. Please note that undergraduate degree transcripts will not be accepted. We require the original documents which do not need to be translated into English.'
Unconditional offer letter from one of your three chosen UK courses (uploaded after interview, by the offer deadline)
Your Final Award Letter (FAL) from Chevening and your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your university - both are required before you can apply for a student visa
existing.english_requirement: The application form must be completed in English: 'If the application form is not completed in English, it will be deemed ineligible.' Chevening also publishes that 'Though an English test score is not required for Chevening, strong English skills are necessary to write a successful application, conduct the interview, and apply to a UK university.' Reference letters must be in English. Separately, UK university applications 'typically requiring: A letter of motivation or personal statement. English language test results. Proof of previous qualifications. Academic and professional references.'
application_method: Check your eligibility against Chevening's published eligibility criteria and confirm your country is a participating SIDS country.
Read the Chevening application criteria and preparation guidance.
Research and choose three different eligible UK master's courses using the Chevening course finder, making sure they relate to a national development priority or capacity shortage.

Register via the 'apply today' link on your country/territory page on chevening.org, read and consent to the terms and conditions and Privacy Notice, then register your email address and mobile phone number.
Pass the online eligibility checker (you get four more attempts if you fail but believe it was an error).
Note and keep your unique access code.

Complete each application section: personal details, immigration details, education history (up to 15 entries), work history (up to 15 entries), programmes of study (three UK master's choices), and the essay answers.
Opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship.
Submit; sift against eligibility criteria runs from October 2026.
If shortlisted, upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate at least seven working days before your interview.
Attend your interview at a British embassy or high commission, March to April 2027.
If successful, secure and upload an unconditional offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
existing.selection_notes: Applications are sifted against the eligibility criteria from October 2026, then independent reading committees assess all eligible applications from mid-October 2026 to January 2027. British embassies and high commissions produce shortlists and interview candidates in March to April 2027; results are announced from mid-June 2027. Applicants are assessed on leadership and influencing skills, the ability to build professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes, the reasons for the course and university choice (linked to UK priorities such as promoting growth and prosperity, building climate resilience, strengthening security and stability, and supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies), and a realistic short, mid and long-term career plan. Chevening states: 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited.' The official page does not publish a separate SIDS selection weighting, so the SIDS element appears to be applied alongside the standard Chevening assessment.
existing.best_fit: Citizens or residents of a participating Commonwealth Small Island Developing State who hold an undergraduate degree qualifying them for a UK master's programme, have at least two years (2,800 hours) of post-degree work experience, can commit to returning home for at least two years, and can choose three eligible UK taught master's courses relevant to a national development priority or capacity shortage. Opting in for the SIDS element does not affect your chances of a standard Chevening Scholarship.
existing.notes: Applicants must commit to returning to their home country (country of award) for at least two years after the scholarship ends. SIDS scholars must study on a course addressing a national development priority or capacity shortage. The award is a one-year master's degree; Chevening publishes no deferral or renewal provisions. Reference letters must be uploaded at least seven working days before the interview - 'Failure to do so will result in your application no longer being considered for a Chevening award.' Applicants must not have previously studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship. No clinical or medical restriction is published.
existing.duration: One-year master's degree in the UK
existing.application_period: Opened at 11:00 UTC on 4 August 2026 and closes at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026, for the 2027-28 Chevening Scholarship cycle. Studies begin in the UK in September/October 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for Chevening Scholarships are now open! Applications close at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. 'The deadline for applications is 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. You will not be able to access the online application system after this date.'

scholarships.title: Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarship - University of Westminster

existing.description: The University of Westminster offers two Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarships to students who are seeking asylum in the United Kingdom. Each covers full tuition costs for a full-time master's course starting January 2027, plus a maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months, published on the University's central scholarship listing as 'Full tuition fee plus up to £12,000'. Applications are made by returning the completed application form with required evidence as PDF attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026.
eligibility: You must have an offer from the University of Westminster for a place on a full-time master's course starting in January 2027
You must be resident in the UK

You must hold one of the following eligible immigration statuses before submitting your application: UK asylum seeker; UK discretionary leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application); UK limited leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application)
existing.eligibility_summary: UK residents seeking asylum, or holding discretionary or limited leave to remain following an asylum application, who hold a Westminster offer for a full-time master's course starting January 2027 and are not eligible for taught postgraduate student loans.
benefits: Maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months (published on the central scholarship listing as 'Full tuition fee plus up to £12,000')
coverage: Full tuition fees for a full-time master's course starting January 2027
Maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months
requirements: Please return your completed application form including required evidence as pdf attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk
Use the University's own application form (PDF, published as 446.67 KB)
documents: Completed University of Westminster Sanctuary Scholarship application form
Required evidence, submitted as PDF attachments alongside the application form
application_method: Secure an offer from the University of Westminster for a full-time master's course starting in January 2027
Download the Sanctuary Scholarship application form (PDF) from the official scholarship page
Complete the application form and assemble the required evidence
Return the completed application form including required evidence as PDF attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026
existing.best_fit: People who are seeking asylum in the UK, or who hold UK discretionary or limited leave to remain as a result of an asylum application, and who hold or can obtain an offer for a full-time master's course at the University of Westminster starting January 2027, and who cannot access taught postgraduate student loans from Student Finance.
existing.notes: The published exclusion list is explicit and disqualifying: students who already have a master's degree are not eligible to apply; students who are able to receive taught postgraduate student loans from Student Finance are not eligible; and the following categories of students are not eligible - Postgraduate Diploma, professional courses (eg RIBA pt III, ACCA, CIMA, CiLEX), conversion courses (eg Graduate Diploma in Law), and integrated masters/MPhil. Only two awards are available. The award is tied to a January 2027 course start, so it cannot be deferred to a later intake on the published terms. No renewal, return-home obligation, clinical restriction, tax treatment, document size limit, accepted file type beyond 'pdf attachments', translation rule or issue-date rule is published on the official pages read. The University also runs a separate one-place Westminster Sanctuary Scholarship for a student granted Indefinite Leave to Remain or Discretionary Leave to Remain, which is a different award and is not recorded here.
existing.duration: Full-time master's course starting January 2027; maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months
existing.application_period: Open for applications for January 2027 entry at the time of verification on 2026-10-01, with a published deadline of Monday 2 November 2026 at 5pm. The University publishes no separate opening date for this cycle.
